task: Upgrade or migrate CodeMie's A2A protocol client/server to the latest published version (or the official a2a-sdk), preserving auth, credentials, assistant execution, and chat history, and resolving the A2UI a2a-sdk pin conflict if the SDK path is chosen.

key_reasoning.reason: Spans the API/router layer, an entirely in-house protocol/domain layer (~8 files: types, utils, client/*, server/*), the security layer (auth/Ability preserved), and the persistence layer (Task SQLModel) — plus the ticket's own framing as an 'upgrade or migrate' of this subsystem, which is the explicit Component Scope red-flag trigger.

AC1 leaves the target protocol version and implementation approach (in-house upgrade vs a2a-sdk migration) as an open decision to be made and documented as part of the work; AC6's backward-compatibility mechanism for previously connected agents has no existing design to point to. This is an architectural decision left unmade, not a minor gap.

Current wire shapes trace to a pre-1.0 A2A draft while the target ('latest published') version is confirmed structurally different (kind- vs type-discriminated parts, message/stream vs tasks/sendSubscribe); server-side streaming is a stub with zero regression coverage; the A2UI a2a-sdk pin is an unresolved, real dependency conflict; and every auth-header branch (Basic/API-key/Bearer/SigV4) plus the recently-fixed public/private discovery split must be reproduced rather than inherited — a security-sensitive, largely irreversible public-contract change.

~10 core source files (types.py, utils.py, 4 client files, 3 server files, router) plus ~2,400 lines across 6 existing test files needing rework, plus likely new files for version negotiation/compatibility, a version-constants module, and new streaming tests — pushes past the 16-modified/6-new XXL threshold, especially if Task/Message/Artifact persistence fields also need to change shape.

If the SDK path is chosen, a2a-sdk becomes a direct, heavyweight dependency with a real, currently-unresolved version conflict against a2ui-agent-sdk's transitive pin (>=0.3.0,<0.4.0, resolved 0.3.26) — matching 'one heavyweight dependency, conflicts possible.'

Touches API, Service (assistant execution), Security (auth/Ability), DB-Persistence (a2a_tasks / Task SQLModel), and External (remote agents, AWS Bedrock AgentCore seam, and a possible new a2a-sdk external dependency) — a cross-cutting, potential-schema-change span across five layers.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from XL to XXL: the ticket explicitly frames the work as an 'upgrade' or 'migration' of the A2A protocol subsystem spanning router, types, client, and server.

Technical Risk bumped from XL to XXL: authentication/authorization behavior (AC5) and stored credentials must be preserved across a public wire-protocol change — an explicit security requirement on a largely irreversible external contract.

Affected Layers bumped from XL to XXL: a protocol-shape change to Task/Message/Artifact fields is flagged in the research as a persistence-layer/migration concern — a potentially significant database schema change.

File Change Estimate bumped from XL to XXL: the same schema/migration concern, combined with ~2,400 lines of existing tests needing rework plus new streaming/compatibility test coverage, pushes the modified+new file count past the 16/6 threshold.

split_recommendation.ordering_note: The version/approach decision (AC1) must land first since it determines the shape of every later slice. Server-side and client-side protocol upgrades can then proceed as independent, parallelizable slices within the same repo. Backward-compatibility and the A2UI dependency-conflict resolution land last because they depend on both the server and client slices reaching their target protocol shape.

slices.title: A2A protocol version & approach decision
slices.scope: Evaluate upgrading the in-house A2A implementation versus migrating to the official a2a-sdk; pick the target A2A protocol version; document the rationale covering effort, maintenance, and the A2UI a2a-sdk pin conflict (AC1). Produce the version-constants/config scaffolding the later slices build against.

slices.title: Upgrade A2A server (task manager, router, agent card) to target version
slices.scope: Update AgentCard/types, the JSON-RPC dispatch in the router, and CodemieTaskManager to speak the chosen target protocol version, including turning on server-side streaming; preserve the discovery-endpoint auth/Ability split and assistant execution path (AC2 server side, AC4, AC5 server side, AC7 server tests).

slices.title: Upgrade A2A client (A2AClient, card resolver, remote agent connection) to target version
slices.scope: Update A2AClient, A2ACardResolver, and RemoteAgentConnections to speak the chosen target protocol version with and without streaming, preserving the four outbound auth-header branches and the existing BedrockAdapter seam (AC2 client side, AC5 client side, AC7 client tests).

slices.title: Backward compatibility and A2UI dependency conflict resolution
slices.scope: Define and implement the compatibility path (or explicit, well-formed incompatibility error) for previously connected remote agents (AC6); resolve the a2a-sdk vs a2ui-agent-sdk version pin conflict if the SDK path was chosen; apply any Task/Message/Artifact persistence schema migration the target shape requires.
slices.depends_on: Upgrade A2A server (task manager, router, agent card) to target version
